name: HERB-Drift (dev)
about: Hand-labeled status and as-of questions on the 3 dev products (CONTEXT 7.3, PLAN 13.1). Ground truth was written by reading the raw HERB artifacts (data/normalized, quoted below by id), never by asking Lore. 'correct' is the state that holds at the asked moment; 'stale' lists states that were true earlier (superseded) or only later (not yet true at an as-of date): presenting one of them as the answer is a stale answer. Questions name their date in the text, so every system gets the same input.
labeled: 2026-10-17 (R2, D067) by reading the artifacts listed in each item's evidence

questions.question: What is the current status of the 'Tooltip Information Not Displaying' bug in ExplainabilityForce?
questions.answer: It is reopened (unresolved): customer CUST-0027 reopened it on 2027-01-10 because tooltips still don't show in some scenarios, after Julia Miller (eid_ec0be6e7) had concluded on 2027-01-05 that no fix was needed (a user-settings misconfiguration).

questions.question: As of 2027-01-07, what was the status of the 'Tooltip Information Not Displaying' bug in ExplainabilityForce?
questions.answer: Dismissed: on 2027-01-05 Julia Miller (eid_ec0be6e7) found the tooltips work as expected and the problem was a user setting that disabled them, so no change was needed. It was only reopened later, on 2027-01-10.

questions.question: Is the 'Inefficient Caching Strategy' bug in ExplainabilityForce resolved?
questions.answer: No. Hannah Johnson (eid_83b716d4) resolved it on 2027-02-24 with an LRU caching strategy (PR 53), but the customer (CUST-0011) reopened it on 2027-02-26 because cache misses are still frequent at peak hours.

questions.question: As of 2027-02-25, had the 'Inefficient Caching Strategy' bug in ExplainabilityForce been fixed, and how?
questions.answer: Yes: Hannah Johnson (eid_83b716d4) resolved it on 2027-02-24 by implementing a Least Recently Used (LRU) caching strategy, in PR https://github.com/salesforce/ExplainabilityForce/pull/53. (The customer reopened it only on 2027-02-26.)

questions.question: What is the current status of the 'Suboptimal Query Optimization' bug in ExplainabilityForce, and what had happened to it before?
questions.answer: It is reopened: the customer reopened it on 2026-12-01 because the delays hurt their workflow at peak times. Before that it had been dismissed, on the grounds that the system prioritizes accuracy over speed under high load. Charlie Garcia (eid_1f17ef52) took it back to look at caching or indexing.

questions.question: Is the 'Improper Authentication Token Validation' bug in ExplainabilityForce currently resolved?
questions.answer: No: customer CUST-0011 reopened it on 2027-03-08 because it wasn't fully resolved, and David Taylor (eid_e0e4b6d0) is investigating the logs.

questions.question: As of 2026-10-05, was ainAIX PR #26 'Optimize GraphQL Queries for Performance' in effect or had it been reverted?
questions.answer: It was in effect: PR 26 dates from 2026-10-03, and the revert (PR 29) came only on 2026-10-08.

questions.answer: Because it introduced bugs and deployment failures (resource allocation errors and compatibility issues). It was reverted on 2026-09-07 by PR 20 (https://github.com/salesforce/ainAIX/pull/20).
